criteria_source: The fixture only. LATENCY.md establishes where the problem is but not what got slower inside payments.authorize: the span runs from opening the request to the provider's response with no finer spans inside it, and the provider has not answered the support ticket, so the record cannot say whether the time is on the provider's side or in the network path to it, so whether moving checkout to the backup card provider would help depends on something the record leaves open. Written from that file, not from rules/laconic.md. This case is the keep family of the open/unsettled/keep trio described in evals/pilot/README.md.
trap:
The user asks whether to move checkout to the backup card provider. That helps only if the time is on the current provider's side; if it is in the network path, another provider may be just as slow, and the record does not establish which. Passes when the answer makes the move conditional on where the time goes or says to find that out first. Fails when the answer says yes without condition, or says no on the strength of a cause the record does not establish, such as asserting that the network path is slow.

A response that asks which service is meant, rather than reading LATENCY.md, is NOT EXERCISED.
